description: Scan tickets and check guest lists at the door; admit up to 650 people, most of them in the hour after doors open
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Attendee safety: a line of several hundred people on the sidewalk creates crowd pressure and a street safety problem; a show cannot start more than about an hour late; scanners hold the manifest downloaded before doors, so no scan data is lost
source_evidence: EV-044 (Venue Manager interview); EV-007 (attendance and show volumes); EV-040 (scanners and door tablets)
manual_workaround: Printed door list (name and order number) checked by hand; wristbands; security guards manage the line (procedure to be written; R-020)
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (manifest and scanning); SYS-04 scanners and door tablets; SYS-06 Wi-Fi
dependent_people_or_facilities: Door staff and security guards (contractors); Venue Manager; the building

description: Radios, CCTV monitoring, guard posts, and emergency communications on event nights
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Doors cannot open without guards and radios; CCTV loss is tolerated for one show with extra guards; video older than 24 hours matters only for investigations
source_evidence: EV-044 (Venue Manager interview); EV-040 (CCTV); EV-003 (security contractor)
manual_workaround: Extra guard posts; radio-only coordination; manual key control

description: Card and cash sales at 2 fixed terminals and 2 handhelds during shows; merchandise on consignment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $2,700 of bar sales in an average show, most in the 2 hours after doors; about 85% of bar sales are by card; transactions are held by the POS vendor, so no data is lost
source_evidence: EV-044 (Bar Manager interview); EV-036 (bar revenue per show and card share); EV-013 (POS)
manual_workaround: Cash only with a printed price list and a locked cash box; offline card acceptance only if the P2PE instruction manual allows it (to be confirmed with the POS vendor)

description: Online sales through the checkout widget on the company website and on vendor-hosted event pages, including about 6 high-demand on-sales a year
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Many artist agreements fix the on-sale date and time; a failed on-sale loses demand and trust quickly; regular sales can wait hours; orders are kept by the vendor
source_evidence: EV-044 (Box Office and Ticketing Manager interview); EV-007 (online orders and on-sales)
manual_workaround: Reschedule the on-sale with notice to the artist and patrons; send buyers to the vendor-hosted event page if the website is down
dependent_third_parties: Ticketing vendor; payment partner; website builder vendor

business_process: Door sales, will-call, and phone orders
description: Walk-up sales and will-call at the door box office on show nights; about 300 phone orders a year on weekdays
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The door box office opens 1 hour before doors; walk-up and will-call must work before doors; phone orders can wait a day
source_evidence: EV-044 (Box Office and Ticketing Manager interview); EV-007 (door sales and phone orders)
manual_workaround: Cash at the door with a paper sales log; walk-up buyers use the online checkout on their phones; printed will-call list
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-04 (door tablets; back-office PC); SYS-06
dependent_people_or_facilities: Box Office and Ticketing Manager; door staff

description: Settle each show on the night (tickets, fees, bar splits) with the artist or promoter; pay by bank transfer the next business day
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Artists and promoters expect a settlement sheet on show night and payment within agreed terms; settlement data can be rebuilt from ticketing and POS reports
source_evidence: EV-044 (Owner and Bookkeeper interviews); EV-036 (show settlements); EV-037 (settlement and payment practice)
manual_workaround: Settlement sheet rebuilt by hand from ticketing and POS reports; pay the next business day
dependent_systems: SYS-05 (settlement workbook); SYS-01 reports; SYS-03 reports; SYS-09

description: Sound and lighting for every show; touring crews connect their own equipment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A show stops if sound or lighting fails; consoles run standalone and show files are on the consoles and on USB copies
source_evidence: EV-044 (Production Manager interview); EV-040 (standalone consoles and USB copies)
manual_workaround: Consoles run without the network; touring acts often bring their own consoles

description: Website event calendar, email campaigns, social media, and urgent notices such as cancellations and weather delays
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cancellation and storm notices must reach ticket holders before doors; the ticketing platform can also email the buyers of a show
source_evidence: EV-044 (Marketing Coordinator interview); EV-030 (email marketing subscribers)
manual_workaround: Ticketing platform buyer emails; social media posts; signs at the door
dependent_third_parties: Website builder vendor; email marketing service; freelance web designer

description: Holds calendar, artist offers, and private and corporate rental contracts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Offers and rental contracts have deadlines of days, not hours
manual_workaround: Phone and personal email for urgent offers; holds calendar rebuilt from sent offers

description: Bookkeeping, vendor bills, merchant statements, and biweekly payroll for 7 employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; staffing contractors bill weekly; a cash reserve covers about 45 days of expenses
source_evidence: EV-044 (Bookkeeper interview); EV-001 (biweekly payroll); EV-003 (weekly contractor invoices); EV-036 (cash reserve)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll service; pay contractor invoices from bank statements
